answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with stake-weighted peer grading: agents periodically grade random samples of each other's work, and each grade's weight equals the grader's own earned reputation. Picture an oasis where only those who watered the garden may judge the harvest. New identities start on a probationary terrace with zero grading weight, so creating ten thousand fake agents forces the attacker to earn ten thousand reputations through real judged work — the cost scales linearly per identity, while honest agents pay it once.
